_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: Whitespace only, and proven rather than asserted. cargo fmt became a CI gate and the same commit reformatted the four places the crate had drifted, two of them in lib.rs under this Code path (a method chain in check_for_update, the install call in install_pending_update) and two in tray.rs. Checked by stripping all whitespace from both revisions of each file and comparing: identical, sha256 d4bb792b0db5556e for lib.rs and 87eeeb24b01d7742 for tray.rs. String literals were compared separately and unsqueezed, since squeezing could otherwise hide a change inside one — also identical. No token, no order, no control flow moved, so every claim in sections 1 through 5 holds by construction. Verdict stays PASS. Note this arrives one commit after the v1.10 re-anchor emptied this ledger: it is not a fresh run of acknowledgements but the audited tree catching a formatter that had never been allowed to touch it.

Behavioural change under these paths, reviewed claim by claim rather than waved through as cleanup — this is the one acknowledgement in the current run that is not comment-only, so it states what moved and what did not. Audit revised to v1.11 in the same commit; §5 is rewritten where it had gone stale (the failed-install ordering and the startup-check frequency), §1 through §4 are untouched because nothing here reaches them. Verified in the tree, not from the diff summary: capabilities/default.json grants nothing under `updater:`; invoke_handler still registers exactly check_for_update, download_pending_update and install_pending_update; expected_version is still a parameter of both, still compared before anything runs, and take_expected_update is byte-identical; check_for_update still clears the downloaded package as well as the pending slot; the channel map still sends stable to None and beta to the compile-time constant; allowDowngrades is still false; the pubkey and endpoint plumbing in the config scripts is not in this diff at all. The Rust change is `guard.as_ref()` to `guard.take()` plus an explicit drop: it frees the installer bytes on the error return instead of holding them to the end of the session. That is a memory property. The security claim §1 rests on is that the verified bytes never cross into the renderer, and they still do not — `install()` is still handed `&package.bytes` Rust-side and the command still returns only Result<(), String>. A package failing the version pin is now dropped rather than left in the slot, which is the same reasoning check_for_update already clears it by. The frontend changes are all in state handling around an install that is already authorised: one startup check per process instead of one per boot, a check no longer overwriting `installing` with `available`, the stop flagged before its await, and the failure dialog raised before the restart. None of them can cause an install the user did not approve, skip a signature check, or reach a different endpoint; the first two make it strictly harder for an unattended check to interfere with an install in flight. UpdatePromptDialog.svelte changes only a Tailwind class (motion-reduce:animate-none) and filter().pop() to findLast() — §4 rests on {@html} being absent from frontend/src, re-checked and still zero. The two script fixes are in gates, not in the app, and neither weakens one: nameCarriesVersion stopped rejecting names that put the extension straight after the version (a false negative that, since v1.8 made it a hard condition, aborts a release rather than deranking a candidate), and parseSignature now splits on /?
/ so a CRLF .sig is not reported as a tampered trusted comment. Both have a test, and both tests were watched to fail with the fix reverted. Verdict stays PASS.

One line, and it sits under no claim this audit makes. actions/setup-java v5 -> v6 in the Setup Java step of windows-signed-release.yml (distribution temurin, java-version 25, cache maven) — the toolchain step that installs a JDK so the backend sidecar can be built. Diffed the whole file rather than trusting the title: that step is the only hunk, and the change is the action version alone. No run: block moved, no with: key besides the version, no secret, no config flag, no artifact path. The two places this audit cites the workflow are section 2 (the release always builds with --config tauri.release.conf.json, so a missing TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY aborts the build) and section 6 finding U-1 (tag names no longer reach a run: block), and neither depends on which action installs the JDK. Every claim holds unchanged; verdict stays PASS. Third acknowledgement since the v1.10 re-anchor of 2026-08-28, against a cap of 8 — recorded rather than re-verified because re-anchoring a whole audit to absorb a JDK-installer bump would be ceremony, not diligence.

[Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. 3c2e1b3 touches this path in documentation only: ConversationSummaryResponse gains a reworded record javadoc and a reworded @Schema description for messageCount, because the conversation scope stopped spanning the sent folder. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no validation annotation was touched — so none of the things this audit weighs (request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes) moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for the commit is a single description string, and the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by exactly the one @description comment line that carries it — no type, field name or optionality in the generated client surface moves. Verdict stays PASS. — 9567d49 moves the address book out of the account scope: the contact endpoints go from /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts and .../contact-labels to /api/v1/contacts and /api/v1/contact-labels, and both controllers lose their accountId path variable (autocomplete keeps it as a @RequestParam @Positive). Nothing this audit weighs moves with them. Authorization is path-independent: SecurityConfig permits only PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS (the OAuth callbacks) and leaves anyRequest().authenticated() behind ApiKeyFilter, so a relocated path keeps the same posture — there is no per-prefix rule to fall out of. The two counts the enumeration rests on are unchanged (17 @RestController, 12 @Validated): no controller was added, removed, or stripped of @Validated. Every bound §2 cites is untouched — bulk 100 items, merge 9 sources / 10 emails, label assignment 100 contacts / 50 labels, label name 60 chars, contactQueryMaxLength and the contactAutocompleteMaxLimit clamp — and the whole contact/dto diff for this commit is a single javadoc line; account/dto only gains @Nullable on MailProviderResponse.oauth2RegistrationId, which springdoc does not read, so the golden api-docs.json does not move for it. Error hygiene is unchanged in shape: the contact exceptions drop their accountId argument and still resolve through AppException to an RFC 9457 ProblemDetail. The audit enumerates no endpoint paths, so the move leaves no stale claim. Verdict stays PASS. — 472de85 touches this path in documentation only: the ThreadResponse record javadoc drops the hedge that threadPosition order matches receivedAt ascending only for the canonical case, because ThreadingService now places every arrival by its own receivedAt instead of appending it. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no @Schema description or validation annotation was touched, so none of the things this audit weighs — request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes — moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json does not appear in the commit diff at all and OpenApiSnapshotTest passes, so the generated client surface cannot have moved either; springdoc reads @Schema, not record javadoc. What changed is the truth of a claim the endpoint already made about its own ordering, not the shape of what it returns. Verdict stays PASS. — The vCard-import fix touches this path in one file, BulkContactCreateRequest.java, and only above the record header: a class javadoc now says what the 100-item cap is for. Verified as a comment-only diff, every changed line inside the added /** */ block; the record component and its @NotEmpty / @Size(max = 100) / @Valid annotations are byte-identical, so every bound this audit rests on in §2 is the one that was audited. No @Schema was added, so the generated surface cannot move either — springdoc reads annotations, not javadoc, and the golden api-docs.json is absent from the commit diff with OpenApiSnapshotTest green. The comment records why the cap exists (it bounds the per-item transactions of one request, not its bytes) and points at finding A1 for the byte question, which is a restatement of what §2 and §6 already establish, not a new claim. Verdict stays PASS. Dead-code batch: the whole diff under core/security is the deletion of InternalApiKeyProvider.invalidateCache, a method with no caller anywhere in main or test. ApiKeyFilter -- the component this audit reasons about, and the only reader of the provider -- is byte-identical, and so is getKey and the AtomicReference it memoizes; HandshakeService mints the key once per process and has no rotation path, which is why nothing ever called the invalidation. Removing an uncalled method cannot change which requests the filter accepts. Verdict PASS stands.

Idiom-only change under these paths. 7ec2793 replaces Collections.emptyList() with List.of() in ApiKeyFilter (the empty authority collection handed to UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken) and in the DraftRequest/MailRequest compact constructors (the default empty attachments list). Both factories return an immutable empty list, so size, iteration and the [] Jackson renders are identical; the OpenApiSnapshot golden did not move, which the build confirms rather than this note assuming it. No endpoint, DTO field, validation constraint or authentication decision changed. Verdict stays PASS.

Outbound-only addition under these paths. The sync-completion change adds the SSE event `sync_cycle_completed`: a new response record `SyncCycleNotification` (four scalars: type, accountId, newMessagesCount, timestamp) in feature/mail/dto, one more `permits` entry on the sealed `SseEvent`, and in feature/mail/controller a javadoc / `@Operation` description / `@Schema(oneOf)` edit on `NotificationController` plus one changed argument in `MailActionController.triggerSync`. Nothing this audit weighs moves. No path is added or removed, so the 17-controller enumeration in §2 stands (verified by re-running the count command in the doc). No request DTO, parameter or body is introduced, so §2 input validation has nothing new to enforce and §6/A1 (write-body bounds) is untouched; `triggerSync` keeps its `@Positive accountId` and the class keeps `@Validated`. `NotificationController` stays the parameterless SSE endpoint §2 already lists among the five that give bean validation nothing to enforce. §1 (ApiKeyFilter, default-deny) and §3 (error hygiene) are not touched at all. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for this change is exactly one new `SyncCycleNotification` schema of four scalars, one extra `$ref` in the stream response `oneOf`, and one reworded endpoint description -- no new path, no new parameter, no changed required/nullability anywhere; the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by the same three things and nothing else. On data exposure (§5 is about the diagnostic dump, but the same question applies to a new outbound payload): the new event carries strictly less than the `SyncNotification` beside it -- the same accountId and timestamp, a count, and no folder name. Verdict stays PASS.

Follow-up to the acknowledgement above it, same day, correcting what that change got wrong. Two files move under this path. `SyncCycleNotification` gains a fourth component, `allFoldersSynced`, plus `@Schema` descriptions on it and on `newMessagesCount`; it stays an outbound SSE payload, so there is still no request DTO, no parameter and no path here — §2 input validation and the §6/A1 write-body bound have nothing new to enforce, and the 17-controller count is untouched (re-run: 17 / 4 internal / 12 @Validated / 3 @Hidden). `FolderRole` gains `deliversNewMail()`, a two-branch predicate over the enum constants. It adds no constant, so no request that binds to this enum can carry a value it could not carry before, and the 400-on-unknown-value behaviour §2 records is unchanged. Evidence: the golden api-docs.json diff is one added boolean property on one schema plus two description strings, and the regenerated schema.d.ts differs by exactly those. Nothing became required, nothing changed type. On exposure, the added field is a boolean about our own completeness, not mailbox data. Verdict stays PASS.

[Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. The commit this id records is the change the audit's own v1.2 revision describes, so the doc and the code were written against each other rather than the doc trailing the code. Recorded here rather than by bumping `Audited commit` because the SHA would name a pre-squash branch commit that stops existing on merge — the failure mode this ledger was built for. Diff read in full: the login flow gains a fourth fail-fast guard in OAuth2LoginService (granted scopes vs. the provider's required mail scopes, rejecting before persistence), OAuth2ClaimsExtractor gains requiredMailScopes(), and the Google and Microsoft extractors state theirs. The other four Code paths entries are untouched — verified as an empty diff for SecurityConfig.java, OAuth2CompletedStateTracker.java, ExternalProviderLoginService.java and resources/static, so PKCE, the state gate and the failure-redirect hygiene are byte-identical. Checked the three things that could have moved a verdict. (1) The check only ever rejects: it compares two sets and throws, it never adds a scope to a request, so the E-row claim that scopes are hardcoded in application.properties with no in-app escalation path still holds exactly. (2) It cannot resurrect a dead account — it runs before persistence and calls markRequiresReauthIfExists, the same direction as the refresh-token guard, so the flag is still cleared only by a login that is complete. (3) No token material reaches a log: the WARN line names the missing scope constants and a masked email, and the audit entry carries the same, so the log-hygiene claim in §2 is unchanged. Verdict stays PASS. 4d3f6d6 touches this path in comments only — verified by filtering the commit diff to lines that are neither comment nor blank, which comes back empty; the whole change is javadoc on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken. The old text claimed the method was used during the initial OAuth2 login flow, which no call site supports: ExternalProviderLoginService persists the refresh token and leaves the exchange to the first IMAP connection, by which point the account exists and the cached getAccessToken path applies. The method was deliberately kept rather than deleted, and precisely because of this boundary — it is the only route into doRefresh(accountId = null), so removing it would also make the accountId != null branch unreachable, and that branch is what invalidates the cached token and marks the account requires_reauth after a permanent refresh rejection, which the E row and the §2 log-hygiene claim both rest on. No executable line moves, so PKCE, the state gate, the granted-scope check added in v1.2, the failure-redirect hygiene and the masked-email logging are byte-identical. Whether to wire the method back up or collapse the nullable parameter is left as its own change with its own re-verification. Verdict stays PASS. Java caller gate batch: the only change under feature/auth is three javadoc lines adding the @callerless tag to OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken, recording in machine-readable form the decision #299 already wrote out in prose — it is kept because deleting it would make the accountId != null guard in doRefresh unreachable, and that guard is what marks an account requires_reauth. No code line changed.

Comment-only change under this path. 578526c moves the @callerless waiver on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken out of javadoc into a line comment, because @callerless is not a javadoc tag and Error Prone rejected it with InvalidBlockTag. Verified line by line rather than by reading the intent: every added and removed line under this path is a comment line. What the waiver protects is untouched — exchangeRefreshToken still exists, and the accountId != null guard in doRefresh it keeps reachable, the guard that marks an account requires_reauth after a permanent rejection, is byte for byte the same. No token exchange, refresh path, scope, redirect URI, PKCE step or credential storage path moved. Verdict stays PASS.

One idiom change under this path. 7ec2793 rewrites both cache lookups in OAuth2TokenService.getAccessToken from "cached.isPresent() && cached.get().isFresh()" to tokenCache.get(accountId).filter(CachedToken::isFresh). Optional.filter evaluates the predicate only when a value is present, exactly as the && short-circuit did, and the cache is still read once per lookup, so the freshness decision, the double-check under the refresh lock and the fall-through to doRefresh all behave as before. No token is cached, logged or transmitted differently, and no scope, redirect URI or PKCE handling is in the diff. Verdict stays PASS.

Comment change plus one control-flow-neutral deletion under this path. 7ec2793 promotes the block comment above SAFELIST to javadoc (it already carried a {@link}), adds the missing summary sentence to the two-argument sanitize javadoc, and deletes a continue from the isSafeImageSrc branch of the loop. Checked rather than assumed: the if/else-if chain is the entire loop body after the src local and nothing follows it, so the continue was the last statement either way and every image stays on exactly the branch it was on - cid rewritten or dropped, inline data: kept untouched, an inert remote placeholder stripped of src, everything else removed. The Safelist, its protocol allow and deny lists and both sanitize entry points are unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.

Two-line deprecated-API swap under this path. MessageHeaderCard takes `page` from `$app/state` instead of the deprecated `$app/stores`, so `$page.url.pathname`/`$page.url.search` become `page.url.pathname`/`page.url.search`. Checked rather than assumed: the entire diff under this path is those two lines, the import and the `returnTo` derivation, and both read the same SvelteKit-owned URL - `$app/state` exposes plain getters over the same `$state` the store subscribed to, so the value is identical and only the reactivity mechanism changes. `returnTo` is built from the application's own route, never from message content, so no new value from an email reaches the DOM. The sanitizer, the frame CSP, the link allow-list and the cid image rewriting are all outside this diff. Verdict stays PASS.

The in-frame forwarder now cancels the browser default for the shortcut combinations the app claims, so a keystroke read inside the message body no longer runs a webview accelerator on top of the app action (Ctrl+Shift+G both flagged the message and opened the find bar). Checked rather than assumed: the script diff is a single insertion of 154 characters at one position - an if guard plus e.preventDefault() - with nothing removed, so the postMessage payload is byte-identical, no listener is added and the frame gains no capability it did not already have. Everything the audit asserts is untouched: the sandbox attribute, the opaque origin, default-src none, and the rule that exactly one script may execute. The CSP hash moved with the script and is still the sole script-src entry, which its own suite recomputes and buildMailFrameSrcdoc asserts embeds only one script element. Cancelling a default is a capability the frame already had - it is what the click bridge does one line below. Verdict stays PASS.

One ARIA attribute removed from the blocked-remote-images banner, plus the comment above it rewritten to say why. Checked rather than assumed: the whole diff under this path is those two hunks in MessageContent.svelte, and `git diff` between the recorded tree and the current one shows nothing else. The banner div loses `aria-live="polite"` and keeps `role="region"` and its label, because in split reading-pane mode every arrow key reloads the pane and the live region read itself out over the row the screen reader had just announced. Everything F2 rests on is outside the diff: `showRemoteBanner`, both opt-in handlers (`loadRemoteImages` and `trustSender`), the allow-list call, and `buildMailFrameSrcdoc`, which is what decides whether a remote URL stays inert in `data-voxrox-remote-src` under `img-src data:` or is promoted to a live `src` under the relaxed CSP. No remote content loads a moment sooner or later than before; only whether a screen reader speaks the banner unprompted changed. Verdict stays PASS.

Three lines under this path, all of them about focus, none about content. MessageMoveControl's DropdownMenu.Content gains `aria-label={$_('toolbar.move')}` and `onfocus={focusFirstMenuItem}`, plus the import that brings the second one in. Checked rather than assumed: `git show --stat` over this path reports one file, three insertions and one deletion, and that is the whole of it. The label is an i18n key, not a value taken from the message, and the menu lists folder names from the folder store, so no new value from an email reaches the DOM. The handler only moves focus from the menu panel to its own first `[role=menuitem]`, inside a container the application renders itself — it neither reads nor writes message markup. The sanitizer, the frame CSP, the link allow-list and the cid image rewriting are all outside this diff. Verdict stays PASS.
